name: Canada

meta.title: Study in Canada from India: costs, work permit, PR route
meta.description: Average Canadian tuition for international students in rupees, the living cost amount IRCC asks for, work hours, the post-graduation work permit and the Canadian Experience Class.

summary: Up to 3 years of work after graduation, 24 hours a week of work during term, and a PR route through Canadian work experience.

whyReasons.text: A master's graduate can apply for a 3-year post-graduation work permit, even if the master's lasted less than 2 years, as long as it was at least 8 months long.
Students can work up to 24 hours a week off campus during term, and unlimited hours during scheduled breaks.
One year of skilled work in Canada after graduation can make you eligible to apply for permanent residence through the Canadian Experience Class.
Average graduate tuition for international students (CAD 24,028 in 2025/2026) is much lower than average undergraduate tuition (CAD 41,746).

ug.note: National average for full-time international undergraduates, 2025/2026. Fees vary a lot by province and course.

pg.note: National average for full-time international graduate students, 2025/2026.

living.note: This is the minimum IRCC asks a single student to show for one year of living costs (applications from 1 September 2026). It does not include tuition or travel. Big cities usually cost more.

visaFunds.text: For a study permit applied for on or after 1 September 2026, a single student outside Quebec must show CAD 23,448 for one year of living costs, plus first-year tuition and travel.

duringStudy.text: Up to 24 hours a week off campus during term. Unlimited hours during scheduled breaks such as summer and winter holidays.

afterStudy.text: Post-graduation work permit: up to the length of your program if it was under 2 years, or 3 years if it was 2 years or longer. Master's graduates can get 3 years if the program was at least 8 months. Since 1 November 2024 most applicants must also show language test results.

pr.text: Canadian Experience Class: at least 1 year (1,560 hours) of skilled work in Canada in the 3 years before you apply. Work done while you were a full-time student, including co-op terms, does not count.

scholarships.name: Scholarships listed on EduCanada
scholarships.text: The Government of Canada lists scholarships open to international students, including programmes for students from India.

faq.q: How much money do I need for a Canadian study permit?
faq.a: From 1 September 2026, a single student outside Quebec must show CAD 23,448 for one year of living costs. You must also show your first-year tuition and travel money.

faq.q: How long can I work in Canada after my course?
faq.a: If your program was 2 years or longer, the post-graduation work permit can be valid for 3 years. Master's graduates can get 3 years if the program was at least 8 months long. Shorter programs get a permit up to the program's length.

faq.q: Can I work while I study in Canada?
faq.a: Yes. Up to 24 hours a week off campus during term, and unlimited hours during scheduled breaks.

faq.q: Does part-time work during study count towards PR?
faq.a: No. For the Canadian Experience Class, work done while you were a full-time student does not count. You need 1 year of skilled work after your studies.
